plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single-name mandate.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 25% to favor income and broad index exposure.
Buy META at 5% of the book, adding a top-quality name from the scanner.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation, reduces overall risk, and maintains a cash buffer.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation and low drawdown. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, but still carries market risk, especially from tech exposure.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure while staying within limits.
Reduce SPY to 25% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
Buy META at 4% of the book, adding a high-scoring long setup.
Buy XOM at 3% of the book to diversify and add another strong scanner setup.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a moderate cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for approximately 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces concentration and leverage, but still has exposure to market fluctuations and tech sector volatility.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
Add to SOXL, increasing its allocation to 6%, and SPAL to 6%, leaning into leveraged ETFs.
Buy META at 6% of the book, concentrating in a high-scoring scanner setup.
Add to CRWD, increasing its allocation to 18%, pressing a strong performing holding.
This plan uses leverage and concentration for stretch growth, with strict stop discipline.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretch growth by using leverage and concentration. It carries significantly higher risk, including potential for larger drawdowns and daily decay from leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is critical.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single-name mandate.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30%, to rotate into income-focused ETFs.
Add to QQQ, increasing its allocation to 25%, for broad index exposure and stability.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown over growth.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield and steady distributions. While prioritizing low drawdown, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff, so it's not a savings account.
